newsitem.title: USA: Central Power says Texas agency reduces rate cut.
newsitem.headline: Central Power says Texas agency reduces rate cut.

text.p: Central and South West Corp said the Public Utility Commission of Texas has decided to rehear some issues and modify some of its earlier decisions on the base rate of its Central Power and Light Co subsidiary.

And based on preliminary calculations, Central Power expects the commissioners' rulings Wednesday will result in a rate reduction on an annual basis of about $24 million, a smaller cut than the $27 million reduction in the March 31 final order. The cut will be from provisional bonded rate levels in effect since May 1996.
But the ultimate amount of the rate reduction could be further modified as the rehearing process continues, the utility noted in a statement late Thursday.
The commission action came in response to motions for rehearing filed by Central Power and eight other parties.

The commission also upheld its ruling that Central Power lower its rates by $16 million in 1998 and an additional $16 million in 1999 through "Glide Path" rate reductions. Glide path reductions are those carried out over a given period.
Also, the commission reduced the amount of invested capital at the South Texas Nuclear Project designated as excess cost over market to $800 million from $859 million.
The utility noted it will earn a 7.96 percent rate of return on this amount.

The company said it was encouraged by the "adjustments and the potential for an improved outcome during the re-examination of issues remanded for rehearing," Central and South West Chief Executive E.R. Brooks said.

"However, we continue to be disappointed with the decision to uphold the Glide Path rate reductions in 1998 and in 1999, as well as the use of a lower rate of return for portions of (the nuclear project) invested capital. We will continue to vigorously pursue all remedies."
Central Power said it expects new rates to be established no earlier than November. Refunds are expected to be issued no earlier than February 1998.
In addition, the commissioners approved a settlement on expenses incurred in Central Power's base rate case and other recent cases, the company said.

Central Power has agreed to a recovery through rates of $14 million of the total $20 million of cost originally requested. This includes the expenses of cities that intervened in the case, as well as the utility's expenses.
About $8 million of the expenses will be recovered as an offset to the final rate refund, and an additional $6 million will be implemented as a $2.1 million annual surcharge over three years.
The remaining $6 million was already expensed during the first quarter of 1997.

Among the more significant issues remanded for rehearing were the effects of certain tax normalization requirements and whether Central Power provided adequate information during the discovery process regarding affiliate transactions.
The commission stated it intends to rule on these remanded issues by the end of August.
Central and South West said the commissioners approved the following adjustments to the March 31 final order:
-- Increasing annual revenues by an additional $4.5 million for recovery of nuclear decommissioning costs.
-- Revising the calculation of the consolidated tax savings adjustment, increasing annual revenues by about $3.3 million.
-- Adjusting the return on Central Power's deferred accounting asset, increasing annual revenues by $2.2 million.
-- Reducing depreciation rates, primarily on distribution property, resulting in a $6.5 million reduction in annual revenues and depreciation expense.
((-- New York Newsdesk 212 859-1610))
